0.value:
Makes the identity matrix: an n by n square of zeros with ones down the diagonal.

Multiplying by the identity changes nothing, the way multiplying a number by 1 does - so it is the starting point for a transformation (a 4 by 4 identity is "no rotation, no move, no scale") and the neutral element when you build one up step by step. As a picture it is a single diagonal line, which also makes it a handy mask: it keeps the diagonal of whatever you multiply it with element by element.

SYNTAX:
t.eye <n: int> <dtype> <device>
Default n is 4. It is always square. n is the first number among the
arguments, so a dtype can come with or without it: 't.eye bool' is a 4
by 4 bool identity, 't.eye 6 bool' a 6 by 6.

EXAMPLE:
t.eye 6

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

in (button):
The small button at the top left of the node. Click it, or send it anything, to send the matrix. Nothing else makes the node send.

n (whole number, also an inlet):
The number of rows and columns. Setting it does not send - the metro in the demo clicks the node 10 times a second, so a new n shows at once. 0 sends an empty tensor.

dtype (menu):
The number type. float32 is the default and what most torch operations want. The menu also offers float16, int64, uint8, bool, complex64 and complex128; 'float' is the same as float32, and each name appears a second time with a 'torch.' prefix, which means the same thing. There is no 64-bit float here.

device (menu):
Where the tensor is made: cpu (the default), and mps or cuda when the machine has them. Tensors on different devices cannot be combined, so keep a chain on one device.

requires_grad (checkbox):
Records operations for automatic differentiation. Leave it off unless you are training something. Only float and complex tensors can carry it: ticked with an integer or bool dtype, the node raises an error and sends nothing.

A dtype or device name can also be typed as an argument, after the numbers - for example t.eye 6 bool.
A bool dtype gives true on the diagonal, false elsewhere.

OUTPUTS:

eye tensor:
The n by n tensor.

READING THE DEMO:
The heat_map uses colour 'hot': 0 is black, 1 white, so the diagonal is a white line from top left to bottom right - row 0 is at the top. Each cell prints its value. Type a different n into the node and the square grows or shrinks.

RELATED:
t.diag puts any values on the diagonal (or reads them off). t.zeros and t.ones fill the whole square; t.full fills it with one value. t.tril and t.triu keep the lower or upper triangle of a matrix.
